{{Quote|Greetings, Gentles! It is I, your culinary caretaker Ms. Gormaanda to once again guide your taste receptors on an ethereal journey.|Gormaanda|<ref name="HNN" />}}
'''Gormaanda''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] member of a four-[[Limb/Legends|armed]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and a four-star-rated [[Chef/Legends|chef]]. Thrice the winner of the [[Orto Culinary Academy Award for Engorgable Excellence]], she also [[Author/Legends|authored]] the [[Book/Legends|book]] ''[[Travels with Gormaanda: Cooking in the Core]]'' and wrote a [[Gormaanda's Culinary Corner|cooking column]] for [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]]. She considered her recipes to be affordable and delicious, and in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], when fresh ingredients were not readily available throughout the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Gormaanda included in her column a recipe for [[Glowblue Noodles and Chav]], a modular dish that could feature any one of a number of meats as its primary ingredient.

Gormaanda additionally recorded [[Instruction cassette|instructional cooking cassettes]] that were available in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as late as [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]]. She frequently prepared food in an energetic and animated fashion, and encouraged her viewers and readers to cook with similar fervor. She was also prone to tasting her cooking and squealing with delight; in a cassette demonstrating the preparation of a [[Bantha rump|bantha surprise]] dish, Gormaanda's excitement led her to cook so rapidly that all four of her arms were required to perform the task. The cassette was viewed in 1 ABY by the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Mallatobuck/Legends|Mallatobuck]], who, having only two arms, was unable to keep pace.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Don't forget to tip your FA droids while on Coruscant. They are programmed to blacklist the stingy.|An excerpt from ''Travels with Gormaanda: Cooking in the Core''|<ref name="NEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Gormaanda.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Gormaanda displays a dish of Glowblue Noodles and Chav.]]
Gormaanda, a [[Gender/Legends|female]] member of a four-[[Limb/Legends|armed]] [[Species/Legends|species]], worked as a [[Chef/Legends|chef]] during the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="HNN" /> During her lifetime, she traveled throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] on a cooking-related journey. One of the stops on her itinerary was the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where she became familiar with the [[Programmer/Legends|programmed]] tendency of [[FA-5 valet droid/Legends|FA-5 valet droids]] to blacklist non-tipping customers from their places of employment. Gormaanda wrote a [[Book/Legends|book]] about her experiences entitled ''[[Travels with Gormaanda: Cooking in the Core]]''.<ref name="NEGTD" /> Prior to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], she won the [[Orto Culinary Academy Award for Engorgable Excellence]] on three occasions, and by that year, she had become a four-star-rated chef.<ref name="HNN" />

Also by 22 BBY, Gormaanda [[Author/Legends|authored]] "[[Gormaanda's Culinary Corner]]," a lifestyle column that appeared in [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] [[Holofeed/Legends|newsfeeds]] throughout the Republic. When the availability of fresh ingredients in Republic [[Realspace/Legends|space]] grew scarce due to the ongoing [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], she reacted by writing a column that detailed the preparation of [[Glowblue Noodles and Chav]], a dish that could be prepared using any one of a wide variety of meats, or even with no meat at all.<ref name="HNN" /> In addition to writing her [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] News column, Gormaanda recorded [[Instruction cassette|instructional cooking cassettes]]; one such cassette, featuring the chef preparing a [[Bantha rump|bantha surprise]] dish, was viewed on the planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]<ref name="Holiday Special" /> in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]]<ref name="Leland Holiday">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=870#15778940|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-10-12|time=6:13 PM|quote=Wookiee Life Day occurs every 3 years, one of which fell at ~1.5 ABY.}}</ref> by the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Mallatobuck/Legends|Mallatobuck]], who was preparing a feast for the Wookiee [[holiday]] [[Life Day/Legends|Life Day]].<ref name="Holiday Special" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Stir, whip, stir, whip, whip, whip, stir. Come on, faster! All together now! Cooking can be fun!|Gormaanda, animatedly preparing a bantha surprise|<ref name="Holiday Special" />}}
[[File:Whipstirwhip.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Gormaanda became very animated while preparing food.]]
As a four-star-rated chef,<ref name="HNN" /> Gormaanda placed stock in the dining experience of her readers and viewers, and she shared recipes with them that she herself considered to be delicious.<ref name="Holiday Special" /> On at least one occasion, Gormaanda referred to herself as the "culinary caretaker" of her column's readers, and claimed that she would take their taste buds on an "ethereal journey."<ref name="HNN" /> Gormaanda also cared for her fans' pocketbooks and frequently prepared dishes that were affordable for the economically meek.<ref name="Holiday Special" /><ref name="HNN" /> In ''Travels with Gormaanda: Cooking in the Core'', she gave advice to her readers regarding how not to get blacklisted from [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] [[Restaurant/Legends|eating establishments]].<ref name="NEGTD" />

Gormaanda's recipes catered to many different types of beings<ref name="Holiday Special" />&mdash;her Glowblue Noodles and [[Chav (beverage)|Chav]] dish was suitable for both the omnivorous and for those whose metabolism rejected meat, and it accounted for varying degrees of consumer jaw size. Furthermore, its primary ingredient was modular, which Gormaanda believed would be beneficial to her readers while the Separatist Crisis plagued the Republic and wrought havoc upon comestible deliveries.<ref name="HNN" /> Although her dishes were typically designed for a set number of consumers, Gormaanda acknowledged that different beings had differently sized "tummies."<ref name="Holiday Special" /><ref name="HNN" />

Gormaanda prepared food in a very animated fashion<ref name="Holiday Special" /> and encouraged her readers to do the same.<ref name="HNN" /> She frequently tasted her cooking and made positive remarks about it; she was also prone to uttering squeals of joy during meal preparation. In her bantha surprise cooking cassette, Gormaanda stirred, whipped, and beat the dish in a rhythmic and increasingly rapid fashion. She claimed that it was necessary to produce a precise and consistent final product, and that it contributed to a fun cooking experience. However, Gormaanda's own elation caused her speed to crescendo to the point that all four of her arms were required to stir, whip, beat, and taste the bantha surprise. While viewing the cassette, Mallatobuck&mdash;herself possessed of only two arms&mdash;grew frustrated at that point and turned the program off.<ref name="Holiday Special" />

On her four-armed body, Gormaanda had [[Color/Legends|grey]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]], yellow eyes, and greyish-brown skin. Her hair was worn in two high buns and at times fell askew when she was cooking animatedly. Gormaanda's favored cooking apparel included a purple [[shirt]] covered with a white apron, as well as four white [[Glove/Legends|gloves]].<ref name="Holiday Special" /><ref name="HNN" /> Ingredients were sometimes worn on a [[Necklace/Legends|chain]] around her neck.<ref name="Holiday Special" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I suppose I'll just have to be content watching my old beat-up VHS copy of 'The ''Star Wars'' Holiday Special' knowing that Korman must have had a blast cooking with four arms as he screamed 'Stir, whip, stir, whip, beat, beat, stir!' We'll Miss You, Gormaanda!|Bonnie Burton, following the death of Harvey Korman|<ref name="Bonnie">{{OfficialBlog|url=2008/05/30/well-miss-you-gormaanda|text=''We'll Miss You, Gormaanda''}}</ref>}}
[[File:HarveyKorman.png|thumb|left|135px|Harvey Korman played Gormaanda in ''The Star Wars Holiday Special''.]]
The character of Gormaanda first appeared in ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', a [[1978]] television variety show spin-off of the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']]. The role was one of three played in the show by actor [[Harvey Korman]],<ref name="Holiday Special" /> with assistance from [[Mickey Morton]].<ref name="Credible">{{YouTube|video=MNsvzX1bLr0|text=CANTINARCHEOLOGY PART 4 FORTY YEARS OF THE STAR WARS HOLIDAY SPECIAL|channel=@CredibleNerds|name=The Credible Nerds}}</ref> The ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} script refers to the character's lone scene as the "Harvey Korman kitchen segment;" it additionally calls Gormaanda "a female chef who enjoys her own cooking."<ref name="script">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsholidayspecial.com/text/script.htm|text=The Fourth Draft Script - 09/13/78|work=The Star Wars Holiday Special|archivedate=20180611081514}}</ref> ''[[Star Wars]]'' author [[Daniel Wallace]] has asserted that Korman's performance was a parody of [[Wikipedia:Julia Child|Julia Child]],<ref name="Dan">{{Blog|danwallace|54|Endnotes for The New Essential Guide to Droids: PART 3 OF 3}}</ref> a famous chef and television personality noted for her simultaneously instructional and entertaining cooking shows.<ref name="Julia">{{WebCite|url=http://today.msnbc.msn.com/id/3694953|text=Julia Child: bon appétit - Celebrated cook taught America to relish life's bounty|author=Sylvia Lindman|date=2004-08-13|work=MSNBC|archivedate=20121105133633}}</ref> Author [[Bonnie Burton]] has similarly called Gormaanda "the multi-armed Julia Child-in-outer-space,"<ref name="Bonnie" /> and multiple sources have dubbed her the "Julia Child of the Milky Way."<ref name="Bad Feeling">{{InsiderCite|106|I Have a Bad Feeling About This!}}</ref><ref name="Galaxy card">{{Topps|set=1993 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 1|cardname=Typical Wookiee Family|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/75144/cid/5338679/1993-Topps-Star-Wars-Galaxy-19-Typical-Wookiee-Family}}</ref>

After its initial and thus far only airing, the ''Holiday Special'' was heavily panned.<ref name="Comedy Hour">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/magazine/2008/12/star_wars_special200812|text=The Han Solo Comedy Hour! (page 1 of 3)|work=Vanity Fair|archivedate=20200113025908}}</ref><ref name="farce1">{{WebCite|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-nov-16-ca-starwars16-story.html|text=May the farce be with you (page 1 of 3)|work=Los Angeles Times|archivedate=20191115073321}}</ref><ref name="multimedia">{{WebCite|url=http://starwarsholidayspecial.com/multimedia.htm|text=Multimedia|work=The Star Wars Holiday Special|archivedate=20180827065634}}</ref><ref name="Jawa">{{InsiderCite|94|Jawa's Corner}}</ref> Gormaanda's scene has been noted by critics as being one of the program's especially bizarre segments.<ref name="terrifying">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/ref/f20071030/indexp13.html|text=Checklist: 20 Terrifying ''Star Wars'' Moments}}</ref><ref name="Atari thief">{{Blogspot|subdomain=theatarithief|url=2006/12/star-wars-holiday-special-1978.html|name=The Atari Thief|text=The Star Wars Holiday Special 1978}}</ref><ref name="imockery">{{WebCite|url=http://i-mockery.com/minimocks/starwars-holiday/page2.php|text=The Star Wars Holiday Special!|author=RoG|work=I-Mockery|archivedate=20190724085904}}</ref> In [[2010]], an article published on [[Wikipedia:Total Film|''Total Film'']] magazine's [http://www.totalfilm.com website] ranked Gormaanda in seventh place on its list of "30 stupidest [sic] Star Wars characters," attributing the character's scene in the ''Holiday Special'' as the driving force behind the ranking.<ref name="stupid">{{WebCite|url=http://www.totalfilm.com/features/30-stupidest-star-wars-characters/gormaanda|text=30 Stupidest Star Wars Characters - The Farce is strong with them|author=Simon Kinnear|date=2011-11-02|work=Total Film - The Modern Guide to Movies|archivedate=20121024092053}}</ref>

Contrarily, both [[Steve Binder]], the ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} director, and SKot Kirkwood, administrator of the fan site [[Starwarsholidayspecial.com]], have named Gormaanda's scene as one of their favorite parts of the program.<ref name="Binder">{{SWArchive|url=movies/saga/20081117.html|text=Holiday Special: Script and Directors}}</ref><ref name="SKot">{{SWArchive|url=movies/saga/20081121.html|text=Holiday Special: A Site for Sore Eyes}}</ref> Bonnie Burton has expressed her fondness for the character, citing Korman's performance as one of the primary reasons behind her love for the ''Holiday Special''. Following Korman's death in [[2008]], both Burton and Heather McPherson, a food writer for the [[Wikipedia:Orlando Sentinel|''Orlando Sentinel'']], wrote sorrowful blog entries with titles indicating that "Gormaanda" would be missed.<ref name="Bonnie" /><ref name="Sentinel">{{WebCite|url=http://blogs.orlandosentinel.com/features_food_blog/2008/05/harvey-kormans.html|text=Harvey Korman's Chef Gormaanda will be missed|author=Heather McPherson|date=2008-05-30|work=The dish - A food blog by Heather McPherson|archivedate=20080603185705}}</ref>
